claims.text: The powder feedstock is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi.
Maintaining the LPBF substrate at 600–700°C reduces thermal gradients during solidification relative to room-temperature LPBF.
Reduced thermal gradients minimize compositional segregation in cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi.
Reduced thermal gradients minimize residual tensile stresses in cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi.
Reduced thermal gradients minimize defect formation in cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheating-assisted reductions in segregation, residual stress, and defects improve mechanical integrity relative to room-temperature LPBF builds.
Elevated substrate temperature slows the cooling rate during LPBF.
A slower cooling rate promotes more uniform solidification.
More uniform solidification reduces microsegregation of alloying elements.
Rapid cooling and high thermal gradients in room-temperature LPBF generate residual tensile stresses.
Rapid cooling and high thermal gradients in room-temperature LPBF promote porosity.
Substrate preheating at 600–700°C produces approximately a 20% increase in tensile strength relative to room-temperature LPBF.
Substrate preheating at 600–700°C produces a porosity reduction of less than 30% relative to room-temperature LPBF.
Substrate preheating at 600–700°C measurably reduces residual stress relative to room-temperature LPBF.
Conventional room-temperature LPBF of cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi often creates high thermal gradients.
The proposed effects are specific to inert-atmosphere LPBF with substrate temperatures between 600°C and 700°C.
Inadequate temperature uniformity during preheated LPBF may cause grain coarsening.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies a porosity reduction of less than 30%, whereas the falsification rule appears to require a reduction around 30%; the pass/fail threshold is therefore not fully consistent with the predicted range.
